source_caption:
To ensure their deeply personal, highly anticipated screenplay was actually being read by studio executives, unknown writers Matt Damon and Ben Affleck secretly planted a completely wild, fiercely out-of-place sex scene between their two straight male lead characters right in the middle of page 60. After meeting with several major studios who enthusiastically praised the script but never mentioned the glaringly obvious scene, they finally met with an executive who immediately demanded the scene be cut, proving he was the only one who had actually read it. By weaponizing a totally absurd script anomaly as a brilliant litmus test, Damon and Affleck masterfully proved that the most important step in launching a legendary Hollywood career is simply finding the one person who actually pays attention to your work.
⠀
Good Will Hunting (1997), directed by Gus Van Sant, starring Matt Damon, Robin Williams, Ben Affleck. A fiercely brilliant, deeply defensive working-class janitor at MIT desperately struggles to overcome his profoundly traumatic past, eventually finding entirely unexpected guidance from a highly compassionate, grieving therapist who completely challenges him to embrace his massive, untapped potential.

source_details.title: Good Will Hunting
source_details.synopsis: Good Will Hunting is a 1997 American drama film directed by Gus Van Sant and written by Ben Affleck and Matt Damon. It stars Damon, Affleck, Robin Williams, Stellan Skarsgård, and Minnie Driver, with Casey Affleck and Cole Hauser in supporting roles. Set in Boston, the film follows Will Hunting (Damon), a troubled but self-taught genius working as a janitor at MIT, whose talent is discovered by professor Gerald Lambeau (Skarsgård). To avoid jail, Will agrees to study under Lambeau while attending therapy with psychologist Sean Maguire (Williams), which forces him to confront his past and his relationships, including with Harvard student Skylar (Driver).
